newsitem.title: INDIA: Monsoon rains help speedy soybean sowing in India.
newsitem.headline: Monsoon rains help speedy soybean sowing in India.

text.p: More than 90 percent of soybean sowings for the 1997/98 (Nov-Oct) crop had been completed in central India after adequate monsoon rains, industry officials and traders said on Friday.

"Weather is very favourable for the soybean crop," V.N. Shroff, secretary general of the Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA), told Reuters. "The intensity of rain is light to medium which is very favourable for the crop."
The central state of Madhya Pradesh produces 80 percent of the soybean crop.
SOPA officials said soybean planting has been completed on 3.8 million hectares in central India against a target of four million hectares.
In the entire country, five million hectares had been planted to soybeans against a target of 5.5 million.
Rains affected market arrivals in Indore, the hub of the country's soybean processing industry, traders said.
Soybeans were quoted at 10,600-11,000 rupees per tonne, below the 11,600-11,900 rupees quoted at the same time last year.
Export demand for soymeal was dull as availability was low, traders said. Soymeal for export was quoted at $265-$267 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship).
